identity.operation: Configure an xmlXIncludeCtxt with xmlXIncludeSetErrorHandler before xmlXIncludeProcessNode.
identity.condition: The entry creates an XInclude context but never installs its context-specific structured error handler and callback data.
identity.capability: Deliver XInclude errors and forward the configured callback and data to included XML parsing and XPointer evaluation.
identity.consequence: The context-specific structured callback behavior is unreachable for every fuzz input.

requirement: The XInclude-context operation must be able to exercise supported delivery of XInclude and delegated parser/XPointer errors to a context-local structured callback with its supplied data.

assessment.requirement: The XInclude-context operation must make the supported context-specific structured error callback and its data reachable for XInclude errors and their delegated parser and XPointer paths.
assessment.target_route: Finite input supplies a main XML document containing an XInclude element. The entry parses it, creates an xmlXIncludeCtxt, sets flags and calls xmlXIncludeProcessNode. XInclude traversal can report errors; included-document parsing and XPointer evaluation use the same context callback when configured.
assessment.failure_condition: The OLD entry never calls xmlXIncludeSetErrorHandler. xmlXIncludeNewContext zeroes errorHandler and errorCtxt, so no fuzz input can cause this context to deliver errors through its own configured callback and data.
assessment.alternative_paths: The initializer installs only a generic error function. Input bytes control options and entities, not the context's callback fields. The reader pass creates no callback on the XInclude context. A global error route cannot supply this context-specific callback and data.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: New contexts have zeroed callback state.
XInclude errors use the context callback and data.
Included-document parsing inherits the configured callback and data.
XPointer evaluation inherits the configured callback and data.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Initialization installs a generic error function only.
Input bytes supply options and the main XML document.
The complete context-use sequence omits the setter.
The remaining reader and cleanup sequence supplies no context callback.

necessity_evidence.reason: The supplied code supports a context-specific structured error handler, and the complete old entry never installs one. The packet does not supply the configure defaults needed to establish that XInclude and XPointer are enabled by the fixed build recipe. That prevents a keep decision under the static environment.

scope_contract.reason: The added setter configures the same XInclude context type that the target creates and processes.

feasible_trigger.reason: The input format can supply a main XML document containing an XInclude element, and the source has paths for XInclude errors and delegated parsing. But XInclude is guarded by LIBXML_XINCLUDE_ENABLED and XPointer evaluation by LIBXML_XPTR_ENABLED. The build recipe does not state their defaults, and their configure definitions were not supplied as numbered evidence.

evidence.dependency_reason: Shows how input bytes provide the main document.
Guards the XInclude implementation on the enabled feature.
Guards the XPointer path and shows its callback forwarding.

observable_consequence.reason: For any execution that creates this context, zero-initialization leaves its handler and data null. The old entry sets flags, processes the node, then frees the context without installing a handler, so context-specific callback delivery is unreachable.

evidence.dependency_reason: Forwards a configured handler to included-document parsing.
Forwards a configured handler to XPointer evaluation when enabled.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete entry installs only a generic error function and contains no call that sets the XInclude context's structured handler or data. Input bytes control options and entities, not those context fields. A global structured fallback would not configure this context-specific callback and its supplied data.

evidence.dependency_reason: Defines the installed sink as a generic variadic error function.
Shows that the context-specific handler and data are installed through the setter.
Distinguishes a supplied structured callback from the global structured fallback and a generic channel.

identity_preserved.reason: Every check concerns the same context-specific structured callback and data on the target's XInclude context, including their forwarding during processing. No separate execution assertion or unrelated error route is substituted.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Uses the context callback and data for XInclude errors.
Forwards them to an included-document parser.
Forwards them to XPointer evaluation when enabled.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Defines the fixed build recipe without showing configure defaults.

missing_information: The configure.ac defaults and resulting definitions for LIBXML_XINCLUDE_ENABLED and LIBXML_XPTR_ENABLED under the supplied build recipe.
The definitions of XINCLUDE_NS and XINCLUDE_OLD_NS needed to ground an exact finite XML witness.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: Deliver XInclude errors through a structured callback and supplied data stored on the XInclude context, with forwarding to included-document parsing and, when enabled, XPointer evaluation.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Enable the relevant features, create a context for a main XML document, install a structured handler and data with xmlXIncludeSetErrorHandler, then process an XInclude node that reports an error.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The old entry creates the context, sets flags, processes the document, and frees the context without installing that handler or data.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: Context-specific structured callback delivery and forwarding through this target.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: The generic error sink and any global fallback do not install a callback and data on this XInclude context; the reader pass does not configure it.
